Updated assessment using the Beige Book:

- Beige Book corroborates a modest-to-moderate pace of activity across most Districts, with tight labor markets and wage gains in the modest-to-moderate range; price pressures remain modest, consistent with inflation near 2 percent.
- Sectoral nuance is softer at the margin: housing and nonauto retail were mixed-to-weaker, manufacturing showed some signs of slowing, and agriculture remained under pressure; commercial real estate was stable to mixed.
- Reported financial market volatility, political uncertainty, and tariff-related headwinds weighed on sentiment; falling energy prices eased some input cost pressures.
- Lending volumes were uneven, and credit conditions tightened in several business categories—aligning with SLOOS signals of tighter standards for C&I/CRE and softer demand in late-2018/early-2019.

Bottom line: The Beige Book reinforces the FOMC’s patient stance and tempers the otherwise solid labor/inflation backdrop. Relative to the prior view, this nudges the tone closer to neutral. Adjusting slightly lower from the earlier 0.20 to reflect softer breadth and tighter credit.
